And now I parent the face com to the null. Just make sure the layer is set to 3D. After making it 3D, I adjust its position manually to get the perfect alignment. Now when I play, you can see the face is perfectly stuck to the orange and moves along with it just like it's glued on. To make our animation better, let's create a funny little story. We could animate it [...] At the end of the animation, I increase the scale a bit. Then set it to zero after five frames. Also, I add a slight rotation and key frame it to finish around the same time. You can rise the position slightly at the end too. No need to track this glow. Manual key frames work fine if you want precise control. If needed, you can use row across time for the position key frames so it doesn't pause at the end. Then I add a glow effect. Increase the radiance and duplicate the glow effect to intensify the shine. As you can see, the yellow appear behind the orange. To fix that, I create a shape layer. go into the faint layer and copy the path from the mask we used for the outline. Then I paste that path into the new shape layer. After converting it to a basier path, I make the shape layer 3D and [...] it to a basier path, I make the shape layer 3D and parent it to the same null that controls the orange movement. I might scale it up slightly to match the orange size. Let's rename this layer. And the track mat section, set it to be masked by the top layer. Make sure it's set to invert. If it looks wrong, just notch the mask slightly to adjust the edges. The more precise you are, the better your animation will look. Now, I finalized the animation and to make the whole thing more lively and fun, I've added a few sound effects.
